name: 48887-partialloradecode-qwen34b-1gpu
model: Qwen/Qwen3-4B (public, ungated, bfloat16), served with the public LoRA adapter `nissenj/Qwen3-4B-lora-v2` (rank 8, alpha 32), which names `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` as its own `base_model_name_or_path`.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of one a3 node.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One rank, one card, no sharding of any kind.
architecture: Dense Qwen3 decoder (Qwen3ForCausalLM): 36 layers, hidden 2560, GQA of 32 query heads over 8 KV heads at head_dim 128, bfloat16; ~4.0 B parameters, 8.04 GB of weights.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=8, warmup 5% and cooldown 5% (both `mode: requests`), bounded at 320 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, seed static 48887.
workload: `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix buckets: exactly 512 prompt tokens and exactly 128 output tokens (min == max on both), greedy (`request_format: plain`, `temperature: 0.0`), `ignore_eos` so every reply runs to its cap, unique synthetic prompts with prefix caching off. Every request is addressed to the adapter, attached in `scenario.json` as `qv1`.
purpose: A fine-tuned 4B chat assistant answering 512-token prompts with 128-token replies for eight concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# Launch config for 48887-partialloradecode-qwen34b-1gpu.
# Every key here goes straight into AsyncEngineArgs at commit 3e90d015ba5b.

model: Qwen/Qwen3-4B

tensor-parallel-size: 1
pipeline-parallel-size: 1

enable-lora: true
# The adapter itself is named CLIENT-SIDE, in scenario.json `spec.backend.lora_modules`:
# `--lora-modules` is an API-server argument and is not an AsyncEngineArgs key.
max-loras: 1
# Tracks the adapter on disk: its `adapter_config.json` declares `r: 8`.
max-lora-rank: 8

enforce-eager: true
enable-prefix-caching: false

# The workload's worst case is 512 prompt + 128 output = 640 tokens, so 2048 is not binding on any
# request; written out rather than left at the checkpoint's own 40960.
max-model-len: 2048

error.text: our harness cannot attach the LoRA adapter the workload targets
